cur:catacombs-arles-eucharist.summary: Seven arched niches separated by columns each hold a standing, bearded figure; Christ stands at the centre among the apostles, several of whom carry offerings. The museum's name, 'the Eucharist', reflects the offering of gifts that runs through the procession.
facts: The museum calls it the 'Eucharistic sarcophagus' and dates it to the end of the 4th century.
cur:catacombs-arles-eucharist.notes: The identification of the central figure as Christ and of the Eucharistic theme follows the museum's naming; the figures are worn.

cur:monumental-santa-maria-in-domnica-ar.summary: At the summit of the arch above the apse, Christ is enthroned within a mandorla between two angels, while the twelve apostles stride towards him from both sides across a green ground; Moses and Elijah stand in the spandrels below. Seen together with the Virgin and Child in the apse beneath, the arch presents Christ in glory as the goal of the apostles' mission.
facts: Wikipedia describes the arch as showing Christ with two angels and the twelve apostles, with Moses and Elijah below, as part of Paschal I's 9th-century decoration.

links.label: Wikimedia Commons: Santa Maria in Domnica - Mosaics

cur:monumental-santa-maria-in-domnica-ar.notes: The photograph shows the whole apse; this entry concerns the arch above it, where Christ is relatively small in the image.

cur:monumental-san-clemente-madonna-nich.summary: In a shallow niche, the Virgin is shown frontally wearing a jewelled crown and earrings like a Byzantine empress, holding the Christ Child before her. The image is faded and damaged, but the imperial costume, also seen in the Maria Regina of Santa Maria Antiqua, presents the Mother of God as Queen of Heaven.
facts: Apart from Santa Maria Antiqua, the lower basilica of San Clemente holds the largest collection of early medieval wall paintings in Rome; the church was buried beneath the new basilica built around 1099–1120.
The figure's imperial regalia have even led some to suggest it was originally a portrait of an empress, such as Theodora, later adapted as the Virgin.
cur:monumental-san-clemente-madonna-nich.notes: Dating ranges from the 6th to the 9th century; the Commons photographer gives the 8th century.
